purpose: Document the strict post-fit failures after adding the Iceland two-sided anchor; this is a diagnostic, not a training target or correction factor.
interpretation: The mechanistic raw Angkor estimate is approximately 603000 people before the England-derived global scale and approximately 205000 after it; the 700000 lower bound therefore exposes a calibration/anchor conflict rather than a missing label.

The Upper Mantaro mapping contains high-altitude locations with many valid structural-zero crop modes; potato/barley/wheat-positive locations remain present. This is a representativeness and historical-crop mapping review item, not permission for a regional multiplier.

The Iceland two-sided interval is failed in opposite directions by the mechanistic and NAM candidates: the mechanistic p50 is below 40000 while the NAM is above 80000. A generic loss-weight change did not resolve both bounds.
Japan Buzen/Tajima are one-sided register floors with partial/non-rice and date-conversion caveats; they should not be converted into point labels.
The Tonga lower-bound failure appears only in some held-out NAM refits; this is challenger instability, not a reason to weaken the lower-bound gate.
tested_generic_variants: combined residual scale and lower-bound weight
decision: Do not implement a loss tweak or anchor-specific/regional multiplier. Keep acceptance blocked until the physical/calibration conflicts are resolved by better evidence or a globally justified model change.
